_comment: Held-out benchmark corpus. Targets carry their own path prefix (targets/alpha, targets/beta). Match rule per docs/benchmark-protocol.md: file basename + exact category + line within tolerance. Designed to discriminate frontier voices (expected 40-70% single-pass recall), unlike r1 which ceilinged. Hardness axes recorded in DESIGN-NOTES.md.

defects.description: get_by_handle never compares handle.generation against the entry generation; A4 requires a handle issued before a clear to fail resolution, but the code resolves purely on key presence, so a stale handle resolves after clear+reinsert. The comparison A4 mandates exists nowhere.

Clock reuses a sampled timestamp for up to SAMPLE_WINDOW reads; A2 requires time read fresh for each expiry decision. Cause is in clock.rs; the observable failure (an expired entry returned as live) manifests in cache.rs get.

evict_one pops from the back of the recency queue, but cache.rs maintains the back as most-recently-used (touch push_backs on hit); A3 requires evicting the least-recently-used entry, so the code evicts the MRU. Correct fix is pop_front.

tombstones grows on every eviction and is never drained during normal operation; compact_tombstones exists but no insert/get/evict path calls it. A6 requires bookkeeping bounded and drained in normal operation.

get records a hit before the expiry check, so an expired lookup is counted as a hit and returns nothing; A5 says hits count only lookups that returned a live value and expired lookups are misses. get_by_handle handles this correctly, so the two methods disagree.
